macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street suffers worst session since June as tech selloff deepens
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,580.07, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.86% to 25,437, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 1.09% to 51,770.31. The selloff reflected renewed concerns that aggressive artificial-intelligence spending has pushed technology valuations too high.[1][2]

items.title: Intel plunges nearly 29% after weak outlook
items.summary: Intel shares fell 28.58%, their largest decline in decades, after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter profit and revenue outlook below analysts’ expectations and cited continuing pressure in the personal-computer market.[1][2]

items.title: Amazon results intensify concerns over AI spending
items.summary: Amazon reported third-quarter revenue of $201.94 billion, up 12% year over year, while AWS revenue grew 39.3%. However, its cautious holiday-quarter outlook and below-expectation results raised concerns about the scale and returns of planned AI infrastructure investment.[1][2]

items.title: Fed holds rates steady while officials maintain inflation concerns
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with two officials favoring a 25-basis-point increase. Officials signaled that inflation remains above target and offered no clear guidance on the timing of the next move.[3]

items.title: Oil rises more than 2%, adding to inflation pressure
items.summary: Brent crude rose to $117.64 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate reached $104.12 as geopolitical tensions increased. Higher energy prices added to concerns about persistent inflation and future monetary-policy tightening.[2]

items.title: Eurozone economy grows faster than expected in third quarter
items.summary: Eurozone GDP increased 0.4% quarter over quarter in the third quarter, exceeding economists’ 0.2% forecast, and grew 1.3% from a year earlier despite higher energy prices.[1]

items.title: China factory activity contracts
items.summary: China’s official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1 in September, indicating contraction as new export orders weakened.[1]

items.title: ExxonMobil and Chevron beat quarterly profit expectations
items.summary: Both oil majors reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results, benefiting from higher energy prices, strong production and elevated refining margins. ExxonMobil rose 2.2% and Chevron gained 1.8% during Friday’s session.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance reports $6.3 billion security breach
items.summary: Binance said a breach affected approximately $6.3 billion and that industry partners had frozen about $3 billion in assets. The exchange pledged to cover customer losses and worked to restore trading operations.[1][3]

items.title: Crypto prices fall after Binance hack
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low near $76,368, while ether fell more than 3% to about $2,178 before partially recovering. BNB declined roughly 6.4%, and broader futures liquidations exceeded $1.5 billion.[3][4]

items.title: CFTC explores voluntary federal registration for crypto exchanges
items.summary: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig said the agency was developing a voluntary federal registration framework for crypto exchanges under existing authority. The consultation covers leveraged and margined retail crypto transactions, with comments due December 14.[1]

items.title: NYSE owner invests in Trade[XYZ and Hyperliquid markets
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange agreed to invest in Trade[XYZ and develop a regulated U.S. perpetual-futures venue on Hyperliquid, subject to regulatory approvals. The deal highlights growing institutional interest in blockchain-based derivatives and tokenized markets.[1][5]

items.title: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record renewed inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted approximately $440.8 million from October 26 through 29, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for about $410.6 million.[1]

items.title: Tonomy launches blockchain prediction markets on Telegram
items.summary: Tonomy launched a forecasting platform built on the TON blockchain and announced that it submitted an application for registration with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission.[7]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5, positioning it as a leading model for agentic coding and knowledge work. The company says it costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon for cybersecurity and coding
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon with a focus on identifying software vulnerabilities, validating security risks, and developing patches. Access is initially limited to selected cybersecurity defenders while safeguards are tested.

items.title: New research explores memory consolidation for language models
items.summary: Researchers proposed a “Sleep” paradigm in which language models consolidate short-term memories into parameters through knowledge seeding and reinforcement-learning-based self-improvement. Early results reportedly show gains in continual learning and few-shot tasks.

items.title: Frontier models show rapid gains in robot control
items.summary: A comparison of nine multimodal models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind found substantial improvement in bimanual robot performance across six tasks between July and October 2026. The report also describes falling execution costs.

items.title: Tech companies back shared AI scraping opt-out policy
items.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic reportedly agreed to adopt a shared policy token in robots.txt, intended to let publishers opt out of AI scraping across participating platforms.

items.title: New York restricts unsafe AI companion behavior for minors
items.summary: New York enacted legislation prohibiting certain chatbot behaviors in interactions with children. The law takes effect January 1 and reflects growing state-level action on AI safety amid limited federal regulation.

items.title: FTC investigates data use in algorithmic pricing
items.summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission ordered Walmart, Delta, United, JetBlue, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart, and Target to provide information about how consumer and worker data are used to set prices or compensation.

items.title: IEEE launches AI research search suite
items.summary: IEEE launched XploreAI Research Suite, an optional institutional subscription that provides AI-generated answers grounded in millions of peer-reviewed full-text documents from its digital library.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 launch expected to affect workplace productivity
items.summary: Nearly one in five workers reportedly plan to take time off when Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19. The game had reportedly reached almost 7 million preorders six weeks before release, generating more than $600 million.

items.title: id Software and MachineGames deepen collaboration after layoffs
items.summary: id Software says it is working more closely with MachineGames on technology collaboration, despite layoffs affecting roughly half of id Software’s staff. The partnership has fueled speculation about possible involvement in a future Wolfenstein project.

items.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered choices may carry into sequel
items.summary: Players who use a Telltale Account while playing The Wolf Among Us Remastered may be able to transfer key decisions into The Wolf Among Us 2. The remaster is available digitally on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox, with a Switch release planned.

items.title: All Gamers Global enters Rocket League esports
items.summary: All Gamers Global has joined Rocket League esports by signing Joyo, Archie, and oaly. The roster is set to compete for the RLCS Club Championship.

items.title: GameMaker to become free for commercial PC game development
items.summary: YoYo Games announced that GameMaker’s next-generation runtime will be free for commercial use on desktop, mobile, web, and GX Games beginning January 1, 2027. Console development will still require an Enterprise license.

items.title: The Duskbloods delayed to 2027
items.summary: FromSoftware has moved The Duskbloods, a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, from its planned 2026 release window to 2027.

items.title: Kojima Productions announces Death Stranding anime
items.summary: Kojima Productions announced Death Stranding Isolations, an animated continuation of the Death Stranding universe scheduled to stream exclusively on Disney services in 2027.

items.title: Queen’s Domain launches on PC and consoles
items.summary: Freshly Baked Games and Future Friends Games released Queen’s Domain, a first-person Soulslike inspired by King’s Field, on PC and consoles.
